assessment: All of the reviewers and editors agree that your deep, rigorous, and multidimensional study addresses novel and significant questions, that it will be an important addition to the literature, and that it presents experiments and data that will motivate further study in the field. You have convincingly demonstrated translational modulation of Sox5, Bcl11b, and Rorb by the RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) Pum2 and TDP-43, with thoughtful experiments supporting cell-autonomous effects of the RBPs on the translational regulation of Bcl11b, Sox5, and Rorb. Your in vivo gain and loss-of-function data in a range of genetically manipulated mouse lines, coupled with in vitro neuronal culture experiments, provide strong evidence for the control that Pum2 and TDP43 exert on these key regulators of neuronal diversification during corticogenesis. Thank you for completing such a deeply informative body of work and for discussing the complexities involved so thoughtfully within your paper.
